mainTopic: Who holds of ברירה: רבי יוסי in דמאי and מעשר שני, רבי שמעון in עירוב, and why the wine of כותים may not be about ברירה at all.
overview: This amud asks whether רבי יוסי holds of ברירה, the idea that a later choice can show what was meant from the start. Two sources seem to show that he does: a חבר buying food for an עם הארץ, and redeeming מעשר שני on whatever סלע comes out of the pouch. The גמרא switches the names in both (איפוך). It proves the second switch from the סיפא, where רבי יוסי 'agrees' about a single new coin. Then רבא asks רב נחמן which תנא rejects ברירה even in a rabbinic law like עירוב, and רב נחמן is silent. רב יוסף answers that תנאים argue about it, and after switching the ברייתא, רבי שמעון is that תנא, since for רב יוסף ברירה is all-or-nothing. רבא instead explains that רבי שמעון's strict ruling on the wine of כותים comes from the rule that תרומה must be a 'ראשית' whose leftovers are recognizable. He defends this rule against אביי's challenges from two pomegranates and from a pile of produce. The גמרא also offers another reason, the worry that the flask might burst, and it begins to explain how the רבנן spoke to רבי מאיר by their own view and by his. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Bird offerings are designated by the owner or by the priest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: קינין only get their designation through the owner's purchase or the כהן's action, so that case is not a case of ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a pair of birds becomes designated either when the owner buys it or when the כהן offers it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started on the previous amud. It explains why the bird-offering case does not prove that רבי יוסי holds of ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird offerings (קינין) get their identity as עולה or חטאת at one of two set moments: when the owner buys them, or when the כהן offers them. Because the law itself builds in this designation, nothing is being clarified backwards. So the case is not ברירה, and רבי יוסי can still hold אין ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of bird offerings (one עולה and one חטאת)
The owner's purchase of the birds
The כהן's act of offering the birds
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was meant from the start

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of an answer that began on the previous amud, defending the view that רבי יוסי holds אין ברירה.

phrases.english: rather, either through the owner's purchase,
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence on the previous amud: 'the קינין are not designated except...'

phrases.english: or through the priest's action.
phrases.notes: The כהן's offering fixes which bird is which.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי בִּלְקִיחַת בְּעָלִים, אִי בַּעֲשִׂיַּית כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer, begun on the previous amud, to the challenge from קינין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the case has its own built-in designation process, so it is not ברירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קינין case seemed to show that רבי יוסי accepts ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: קינין are designated by the owner's purchase or the כהן's action, so there is no proof that רבי יוסי accepts ברירה.

steps.title: Challenge from a חבר buying food for an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again whether רבי יוסי really holds אין ברירה. It cites a ברייתא where רבי יוסי frees a חבר from tithing food he bought for an עם הארץ, which sounds like ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still: does רבי יוסי hold that there is no ברירה? But a ברייתא teaches: an עם הארץ said to a חבר, 'Buy me one bundle of vegetables or one roll.' The חבר does not need to tithe it. These are the words of רבי יוסי. The חכמים say he must tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. It quotes a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי seems to accept ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חבר bought several items without saying which one was for the עם הארץ. When he hands one over, we say backwards that this one was bought for the עם הארץ from the start, so the חבר never owned it and does not need to tithe it as דמאי. That reasoning is ברירה, which seems to contradict רבי יוסי's view in the earlier wine case.

keyTerms.meaning: And still (a further difficulty remains)
A person not trusted to separate tithes
A person trusted to be careful with tithes and purity
A fine roll or cake
To separate tithes (here, from דמאי produce)

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים's opinion (he must tithe) is still part of the quoted ברייתא. It is not the גמרא's answer. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַכַּתִּי: סָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֵין בְּרֵירָה?
phrases.english: And still: does Rabbi Yosei hold there is no retroactive designation?
phrases.notes: Opens a new challenge.

phrases.english: But it was taught: an am ha'aretz who said to a chaver,
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: "Buy for me one bundle of vegetables
or one roll" —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְעַשֵּׂר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: he does not need to tithe; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: This assumes ברירה: the item was the עם הארץ's from the start.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: he must tithe.
phrases.notes: The Sages reject ברירה here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי: סָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֵין בְּרֵירָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קינין challenge is answered, the גמרא brings a new source against the claim that רבי יוסי holds אין ברירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוסי holds אין ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי exempts the חבר from tithing only if the item is treated, looking backwards, as the עם הארץ's from the start. That is ברירה.

steps.title: Reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by switching the names in the ברייתא, so that רבי יוסי requires tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse the opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with one word. It switches the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the reversal, רבי יוסי says the חבר must tithe, because he holds אין ברירה. The חכמים are the ones who exempt him. This keeps רבי יוסי consistent with his view in the wine case.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse (switch the opinions in the source)

phrases.english: Reverse [the opinions].
phrases.notes: A one-word answer that switches who holds which view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the חבר and עם הארץ ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: switch the names of the opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי exempts the חבר from tithing, so he holds of ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the ברייתא reversed: רבי יוסי requires tithing, which fits אין ברירה.

steps.title: Challenge from redeeming tithe on an unchosen coin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another source. Someone redeems his מעשר שני on whatever סלע comes up in his hand from the pouch, and רבי יוסי says it is redeemed. This sounds like ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: someone says, 'The מעשר שני in my house is redeemed on the סלע that will come up in my hand from the pouch.' רבי יוסי says: it is redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens another challenge with תא שמע. It brings a case where רבי יוסי seems to accept ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the person makes the statement, no specific coin has been chosen yet. Saying the מעשר is redeemed means that when a coin is pulled out, it becomes clear backwards that this was the coin from the start. That is ברירה, so the question of רבי יוסי's view comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source as proof or challenge)
Here: מעשר שני, the second tithe, which can be redeemed with money
Redeemed (its holiness moves onto the coin)
A silver coin
Pouch or purse

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who says:
phrases.notes: Introduces a new source.

phrases.english: "The tithe that I have in my house
phrases.notes: Refers to מעשר שני.

phrases.english: is redeemed upon the sela
that will come up in my hand from the pouch."
phrases.notes: No specific coin was chosen in advance.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: it is redeemed!
phrases.notes: Seems to assume ברירה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא was reversed, the גמרא brings another source suggesting רבי יוסי holds of ברירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds אין ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redemption works only if the coin pulled out later counts as chosen from the start, which is ברירה. Yet רבי יוסי says it is redeemed.

steps.title: Switch the names in the coin-pouch case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by switching the opinions, so that רבי יוסי says the מעשר שני was not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it, and say: רבי יוסי says he has not redeemed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same trick it used in step 3. It switches the names, so that רבי יוסי holds the מעשר שני is not redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that רבי יוסי seemed to hold of ברירה, because he said the מעשר is redeemed on whichever coin comes up. If we switch the opinions, רבי יוסי says it is not redeemed. That fits his view of אין ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse, switch the names of the opinions
He redeemed, meaning the holiness moved onto the coin
Second tithe, which can be redeemed onto money

phrases.english: Reverse it, and say:
Rabbi Yosei says: he has not redeemed.
phrases.notes: Now רבי יוסי consistently holds אין ברירה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 using the same switching method as step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי says the מעשר is redeemed on whichever coin comes up, which would mean he holds of ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names are switched. רבי יוסי says it is not redeemed, which is consistent with אין ברירה.

steps.title: Why switch two sources instead of one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we switch two ברייתות to match one source, when we could switch the one source to match the two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you reverse two sources because of one? Reverse the one because of the two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the method of switching names. Now two ברייתות have been switched just to fit one source that says רבי יוסי holds אין ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources say רבי יוסי holds of ברירה: the חבר case and the coin-pouch case. Only one source says he holds אין ברירה. So it seems more logical to fix the single source and say that רבי יוסי really holds of ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why choose this way over the other?
Two
One
Because of, in the face of

phrases.english: And what did you see
that you reversed two sources because of one?
phrases.notes: The two ברייתות were switched to fit the one source showing אין ברירה.

phrases.english: Reverse the one because of the two!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חֲזֵית דְּאָפְכַתְּ תַּרְתֵּי מִקַּמֵּי חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the switching method used in steps 3 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to switch the names in the two ברייתות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The majority of sources should win. It is more reasonable to fix one source than two.

steps.title: The סיפא proves this ברייתא must be switched
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says 'רבי יוסי agrees' that a new סלע works. That shows he disagreed in the רישא, so the רישא must read that it is not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא was certainly taught the other way around, because the סיפא says: 'And רבי יוסי agrees about one who says, "The מעשר I have in my house should be redeemed on the new סלע that will come up in my hand from the pouch," that he has redeemed.' Since it says here that he redeemed, this implies that there, in the רישא, he did not redeem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the switch is not a guess. The ברייתא itself proves the original wording must be switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מודה ('he agrees') means רבי יוסי is now agreeing to something he did not agree to before. So in the רישא, where the coin was not clearly defined, he must have said the מעשר was not redeemed. This proves that the correct reading of the רישא is that רבי יוסי says לא חילל.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a source
Agrees, concedes, implying he disagreed elsewhere
A new סלע coin
Pouch, wallet
By implication, you can infer

steps.whyThisMatters: The switch of names is now backed by the text itself, so רבי יוסי's view of אין ברירה stays consistent.

phrases.english: This was certainly taught in reverse,
since the latter clause teaches:
And Rabbi Yosei agrees regarding one who says:
"The tithe that I have in my house
shall be redeemed on the new sela
that will come up in my hand from the pouch" — that he has redeemed.
Since it says here that he has redeemed,
this implies that there, he has not redeemed.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the רישא, the coin-pouch case from step 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא וַדַּאי אִיפְּכָא תַּנְיָא, דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by proving from the text that this ברייתא needs to be switched.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Internal textual proof from the סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Switching the names was arbitrary, and it might be better to switch the one source instead.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word מודה in the סיפא proves that in the רישא, רבי יוסי held the מעשר was not redeemed.

steps.title: What exactly is the new סלע case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the new סלע case works. If there are several new coins, it is the same as the רישא. If there is only one, why say 'that will come up'?
steps.simpleTranslation: This new סלע, what is the case? If there are two or three new coins, so there is a question of ברירה, then it is the same as the first case! Rather, there is only one new coin. But then what does 'will come up' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now examines the סיפא it just used as proof, and asks exactly what case it describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pouch holds several new coins, then which one is meant is decided only later. That is ברירה, just like the רישא, so why would רבי יוסי agree here? But if there is only one new coin, it is clearly chosen from the start, and the phrase 'that will come up in my hand' sounds strange.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was meant from the start
The first case
Will come up

phrases.english: This new sela, what is the case?
If there are two or three new coins,
so it depends on ברירה, then it is the same as the first case!
Rather, there is only one new coin —
then what does 'will come up' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case in the סיפא that step 7 used as proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording and case of the סיפא about the new סלע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ways of reading the case cause a problem. Several coins makes it the same as the רישא, and one coin makes the word תעלה hard to explain.

steps.title: The word תעלה was copied from the רישא
steps.stepSummary: The case is one new coin. The סיפא uses the word 'will come up' only because the רישא used it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the רישא taught 'will come up,' the סיפא also taught 'will come up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case has only one new coin. The extra wording is just carried over from the רישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one new coin, it is clear from the start which coin is meant, so there is no ברירה. That is why רבי יוסי agrees. The word תעלה does not mean there is any choice; it simply matches the style of the רישא.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because of the pattern of
The first clause of a source

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is switched, so רבי יוסי says אין ברירה in the coin-pouch case. He agrees only when there is a single new coin, because then it is clear from the start. Here the word תעלה is just copied from the רישא.
steps.confusionAlert: In the סיפא, 'will come up' does not mean there is any choice among coins. There is only one new coin, so nothing is decided later.

phrases.english: Since the first clause taught 'will come up,'
the latter clause also taught 'will come up.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by choosing the one-coin case and explaining the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word תעלה implies a choice among several coins, which would make it the same as the רישא.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is only one new coin. The word תעלה is borrowed from the רישא and adds no meaning.

steps.title: רבא asks who holds there is no retroactive choice even in rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן to identify the תנא of a ברייתא that seems to reject ברירה even for a rabbinic law like עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Who is this תנא who does not accept ברירה even in rabbinic matters? It was taught: A person said to five people, 'I am making an עירוב for whichever one of you I choose. The one I choose may walk, and the one I do not choose may not walk.' If he chose while it was still day, his עירוב works. If he chose after dark, his עירוב does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. He quotes a ברייתא and asks which תנא would rule that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we accepted ברירה, a choice made after dark could 'reveal' that the עירוב was for that person all along, and it would work. Since the ברייתא says a choice after dark does not work, its author must reject ברירה. That is striking, because עירוב is only דרבנן, where we would expect people to be more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was true from the start
A rabbinic law, not a Torah law
A sage of the משנה period, or the author of a ברייתא
Placing an עירוב
While it is still day, before שבת begins
After it gets dark, once שבת has begun

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether ברירה exists in Torah law. רבא is surprised that someone rejects it even in a lenient rabbinic area like עירוב.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Who is this tanna
who does not hold of retroactive clarification even in rabbinic matters?
As it was taught: He said to five people

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵינִי מְעָרֵב עַל אֵיזֶה מִכֶּם שֶׁאֶרְצֶה,
phrases.english: I am making an eiruv for whichever of you I choose,
the one I choose may walk,
the one I do not choose may not walk.
If he chose while it was still day, his eiruv is valid;
if he chose after dark, his eiruv is not valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of inquiry about ברירה in rabbinic law
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who rejects ברירה even for a rabbinic law like עירוב

steps.title: רב נחמן is silent, so why did he not name the school of איו
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives no answer. The גמרא asks why he did not say the ברייתא follows the תנא of the house of איו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן was silent and said nothing at all. The גמרא asks: Let him answer that it is the תנא of the house of איו!
steps.whatsHappening: The story says רב נחמן had no answer. The גמרא then challenges that silence by suggesting an answer he could have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house of איו reported that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה even in עירוב. That would make רבי יהודה exactly the תנא רבא was looking for. So the גמרא asks why רב נחמן stayed silent when a ready answer existed.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent
But let him say to him (a challenge: why didn't he answer this way?)
The teacher from the school of איו, who reported רבי יהודה's view that there is no ברירה in עירוב

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק, וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything to him.
But let him say to him
it is the tanna of the school of Ayo!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבא's question and challenges רב נחמן's failure to answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known source, the house of איו, already identifies a תנא who rejects ברירה in עירוב, so silence seems unnecessary

steps.title: רב נחמן did not accept the איו report
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן had not heard, or did not accept, the teaching of the house of איו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had not heard it, meaning he did not accept that teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב נחמן could not use the איו answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן did not hold the איו version of רבי יהודה's opinion to be reliable. Without it, he knew of no תנא who rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law. So he stayed silent.

keyTerms.meaning: He had not heard it, meaning he did not accept it as authoritative
The תנא whose view the house of איו reported

phrases.english: He did not accept it (lit. he had not heard it).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source was unknown to him, or not accepted by him
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן should have cited the house of איו
steps.terutzMaskana: He did not accept that report, so he had no answer

steps.title: רב יוסף shows it is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers רבא's question by citing a ברייתא where רבי שמעון and חכמים argue about ברירה in עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Did you remove the תנאים from the world? It is a dispute between תנאים! It was taught: A person said, 'I am making an עירוב for all the שבתות of the year. If I want, I will walk; if I do not want, I will not walk.' If he decided while it was still day, his עירוב works. If he decided after dark, רבי שמעון says his עירוב works, and חכמים say it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the answer רב נחמן could not give. He points to a ברייתא where תנאים argue about this exact issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Deciding after dark can only work through ברירה. As the ברייתא is written, רבי שמעון accepts ברירה and חכמים reject it. That would make חכמים the תנא who rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law.

keyTerms.meaning: Have you removed the תנאים from the world? (Do you think no תנא holds this?)
It is a dispute between תנאים
For all the שבתות of the year
And the Sages (the majority opinion)

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: תַּנָּאֵי שָׁקְלַתְּ מֵעָלְמָא?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Have you removed the tanna'im from the world?
It is a dispute of tanna'im! As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵינִי מְעָרֵב לְשַׁבָּתוֹת שֶׁל כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: I am making an eiruv for the Shabbatot of the whole year,

phrases.aramaic: רָצִיתִי — אֵלֵךְ, לֹא רָצִיתִי — לֹא אֵלֵךְ.
phrases.english: if I want, I will walk; if I do not want, I will not walk.
If he decided while it was still day, his eiruv is valid.
If he decided after dark,
Rabbi Shimon says: his eiruv is valid;
and the Sages say: his eiruv is not valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבא's original question and answers it
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a תנאים dispute. As the ברייתא is written, חכמים reject ברירה even in עירוב.

steps.title: רבי שמעון contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: Elsewhere רבי שמעון rejects ברירה, so how can he accept it here?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we have heard that רבי שמעון does not accept ברירה! There is a contradiction between one statement of רבי שמעון and another statement of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's ברייתא. The way it is written, it clashes with what we know about רבי שמעון from another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of wine bought from כותים, רבי שמעון does not rely on ברירה. In this ברייתא he does accept ברירה. One person cannot hold both views, so something must be adjusted.

keyTerms.meaning: But we have heard (introduces a known contrary source)
A contradiction between one statement and another statement of the same sage
Wine of the כותים, the case where רבי שמעון rejects ברירה

phrases.english: But we have heard regarding Rabbi Shimon
that he does not hold of retroactive clarification;
there is a contradiction between Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Shimon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא cited in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's opinion in רב יוסף's ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rejects ברירה in the case of wine from כותים, but accepts it in this ברייתא

steps.title: Reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses the ברייתא. Now רבי שמעון says the עירוב is invalid, so he is the תנא who rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, reverse the opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by switching who says what in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the switch, רבי שמעון says a decision after dark does not work, which matches his view in the wine case. That makes רבי שמעון the answer to רבא's question: a תנא who rejects ברירה even in a rabbinic law like עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a correction)
Reverse, meaning switch the opinions

steps.whatToRemember: There is a תנאים dispute about ברירה in rabbinic law. After the reversal, רבי שמעון consistently rejects ברירה, even for עירוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רבא's opening question. It also fits the pattern on this daf of switching opinions so a sage stays consistent, as in steps 5–7.

phrases.english: Rather, reverse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the opinions in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון accepts ברירה in עירוב
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון says the עירוב is invalid. He rejects ברירה even in rabbinic law, and this answers רבא's question.

steps.title: Why reverse the ברייתא at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the need for the reversal. Maybe רבי שמעון rejects ברירה only in Torah law but accepts it in rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Perhaps רבי שמעון rejects ברירה only in Torah law, but in rabbinic law he accepts it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 15, where the ברייתא was reversed. It suggests there may be no real contradiction in רבי שמעון's views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction came from רבי שמעון rejecting ברירה in one place and accepting it in the עירוב case. But עירוב is only a rabbinic law. If רבי שמעון rejects ברירה only for Torah-level matters, both rulings fit together and no reversal is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (questioning whether a problem really exists)
Retroactive clarification: a later event reveals what was designated earlier
Torah-level law
Rabbinic-level law

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵירָה
phrases.english: Perhaps when Rabbi Shimon does not accept retroactive designation
it is in Torah law,
but in rabbinic law, he does accept it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the necessity of the reversal made in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reversal of the ברייתא in step 15 and the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The contradiction disappears if ברירה is split by level: rejected in Torah law, accepted in rabbinic law. Since עירוב is rabbinic, no reversal is needed.

steps.title: רב יוסף holds ברירה is all-or-nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף holds there is no split between Torah law and rabbinic law. Whoever accepts ברירה accepts it everywhere, and whoever rejects it rejects it everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף holds: whoever accepts ברירה accepts it, whether in Torah law or rabbinic law. Whoever rejects ברירה rejects it, whether in Torah law or rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב יוסף still needed the reversal. In his view, a person cannot accept ברירה in one area and reject it in another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16's suggestion depends on dividing ברירה by level of law. רב יוסף rejects that division, so the contradiction in רבי שמעון stands. That is why the ברייתא had to be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (introduces someone's underlying view)
There is no difference
He accepts it / he does not accept it

phrases.english: Rav Yosef holds:
One who accepts retroactive designation,
no difference whether in Torah law,
no difference whether in rabbinic law, he accepts it.
And one who does not accept retroactive designation,
no difference whether in Torah law
and no difference whether in rabbinic law, he does not accept it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by rejecting its proposed distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the proposed distinction (ברירה is all-or-nothing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ברירה could be accepted in rabbinic law and rejected in Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב יוסף, ברירה applies equally at both levels, so the contradiction is real and the reversal is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: ברירה is all-or-nothing. If you hold it, you hold it in both Torah law and rabbinic law. If you reject it, you reject it in both.

steps.title: רבא: the wine case has a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי שמעון's strict ruling in the wine case is not about ברירה. It is because תרומה must be a first portion whose leftovers are recognizable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case there is different, because we require 'a first portion whose leftovers are recognizable.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to remove the contradiction in רבי שמעון. It does not require reversing the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'There' refers to the wine bought from כותים. In that case a person declares that the wine he will separate later is תרומה, and רבי שמעון forbids it. רבא says the problem is not ברירה. The Torah calls תרומה 'ראשית' (the first portion), and that requires the leftover part to be clearly identifiable at the time of designation. That is missing here, so רבי שמעון can still accept ברירה, as in the עירוב case.

keyTerms.meaning: The case there is different
The 'first portion', the Torah's term for תרומה
Whose leftovers are recognizable
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is NOT saying רבי שמעון rejects ברירה. He is saying the wine case fails for a completely separate reason, so it tells us nothing about ברירה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is different there,
for we require 'a first portion whose leftovers are recognizable.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the contradiction of step 14, replacing רב יוסף's reversal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (a different underlying reason)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון forbids the wine because he rejects ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון forbids the wine because of the 'ראשית ששיריה ניכרין' requirement for תרומה, so he may still accept ברירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the need to reverse the ברייתא. It also creates a new rule about תרומה that אביי will now test.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא with two pomegranates
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that by רבא's logic, a conditional designation between two טבל pomegranates would mean nothing, because the leftover is not recognizable when the designation is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, suppose there were two טבל pomegranates in front of someone, and he said, 'If it rains today, this one is תרומה for that one, and if it does not rain today, that one is תרומה for this one.' Would you also say that whether it rained or not, his words mean nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's new rule by applying it to a case where it seems to give an unacceptable result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the person speaks, nobody knows which pomegranate is תרומה and which is the leftover, because it depends on the rain. If 'ששיריה ניכרין' blocks the wine case, it should block this case too and make his statement void. אביי treats that result as unreasonable, which suggests רבא's rule cannot be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so (introduces a challenge that follows from the other's logic)
Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated
Pomegranates
His words have no effect

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if that is so,

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁנֵי רִמּוֹנִים שֶׁל טֶבֶל,
phrases.english: if there were before him two pomegranates of tevel,
and he said: If rain falls today,
this one shall be teruma for that one,
and if rain does not fall today,
that one shall be teruma for this one,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי בֵּין יָרְדוּ בֵּין לֹא יָרְדוּ
phrases.english: would you say so too, that whether it rained or did not rain,
his words have no effect?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule of 'ראשית ששיריה ניכרין' introduced in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that תרומה requires recognizable leftovers at the time of designation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the rule would also cancel a conditional designation between two pomegranates, where the leftover is unknown until the rain decides it. That result seems unacceptable.

steps.title: A משנה where רבי שמעון accepts תרומה designated inside a pile
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes further. Suppose רבא accepts that a designation between two pomegranates means nothing. A משנה still shows רבי שמעון accepting a designation of תרומה hidden inside a pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that this is really so, didn't we learn in a משנה: 'The תרומה of this pile and its tithes are inside it,' or 'The תרומת מעשר of this tithe is inside it.' רבי שמעון says: He has given it a name, and it takes effect!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי expects רבא to accept the pomegranate result. So he brings a משנה where רבי שמעון clearly lets a hidden designation take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pile case, the person never says exactly which part is תרומה, so the leftovers are not marked off. Even so, רבי שמעון says the designation works. That seems to disprove רבא's rule that תרומה must be a first portion with recognizable leftovers.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say it really is so (blocking a possible escape)
A pile of grain or produce
The portion the לוי gives to a כהן from his tithe
He has 'called the name.' The designation takes effect.

phrases.english: And if you say, indeed it is so,
but didn't we learn in a mishnah:
The terumah of this pile
and its tithes are inside it,
and the terumah of this tithe is inside it.
Rabbi Shimon says: He has given it a name!
phrases.notes: The designation takes effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's challenge from Step 19. It blocks רבא from simply accepting the pomegranate result.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation (Step 18) that רבי שמעון requires תרומה whose leftovers are recognizable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the pile case the leftovers are not marked, yet רבי שמעון lets the designation work. So recognizable leftovers cannot be his requirement.

steps.title: A pile has clearly non-terumah edges around it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the pile case is different. Saying 'inside it' means the outer edges of the pile are certainly not תרומה, so some leftovers are recognizable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because there is the area surrounding it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his rule. He shows that the pile case actually does have recognizable leftovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Inside it' points to the middle of the pile. The produce around the edges is clearly not תרומה, so the leftovers are partly visible. רבא's rule therefore still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Its surroundings (the outer edges of the pile)

phrases.english: It is different there
because there is its surrounding area.
phrases.notes: The edges of the pile are clearly not תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the pile משנה in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (אוקימתא of the facts)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pile case has no recognizable leftovers, so it contradicts רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pile does have recognizable leftovers, namely its outer edges. So it fits רבא's rule.

steps.title: Another answer: the רבנן only worried that the flask might burst
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different reason for the strict view in the wine case. The ברייתא itself says the רבנן worried the flask might burst before תרומה was separated. רבי מאיר answered that he would deal with that when it happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is like the reason that was taught there. They said to רבי מאיר: 'Don't you agree that the flask might burst? Then it turns out this person was drinking טבל all along!' He said to them: 'When it bursts, we will deal with it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate explanation of why the wine case is strict. This explanation has nothing to do with ברירה or with recognizable leftovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the reason openly. If the flask bursts before he separates the two לוגין, nothing was ever separated, so all the wine he drank was טבל. The argument is only about how much to worry about the flask bursting, not about the principle of designating later.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces an alternative answer)
A leather flask for wine
טבל: produce from which תרומה and tithes have not yet been separated, forbidden to eat
Retroactively
When it bursts (deal with it then)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. The first answer (רבא's) says the problem is that the leftovers are not recognizable. This second answer says the only problem is the risk that the flask bursts. They are two different explanations.

phrases.english: And if you want, say
as the reason is taught:
They said to Rabbi Meir:
Don't you agree
that perhaps the flask will burst,
and it will turn out this one was drinking tevel retroactively!
He said to them: When it bursts!
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר is not worried about it now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second way to answer אביי's challenges (steps 19–20). It explains the wine case by the flask-bursting worry instead of the 'recognizable leftovers' reason, so רבי שמעון can still accept ברירה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reason drawn from the explicit wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The strict view in the wine case comes from rejecting ברירה, or from requiring recognizable leftovers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict view comes only from the practical worry that the flask may burst and leave the wine as טבל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that the wine case does not prove anything about רבי שמעון's view on ברירה.

steps.title: Why didn't the רבנן argue about recognizable leftovers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first approach. If the real issue were recognizable leftovers, the רבנן should have said that to רבי מאיר. Instead they argued about the flask bursting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to what we first thought, that we require a first portion whose leftovers are recognizable, what are they saying to him? They should have argued that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבא's first answer. It asks why the ברייתא shows the רבנן arguing about the flask instead of about recognizable leftovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא records the רבנן's real argument, and it is about the flask bursting. If recognizable leftovers were the key issue, that would have been their main point. Their silence on it suggests the first approach is not the true reason.

keyTerms.meaning: According to what we first thought
A 'first' portion whose leftovers are recognizable
What are they saying to him? (Why argue this point instead?)

phrases.english: And according to what initially entered our minds
that we require a "first" portion
whose leftovers are recognizable,
what are they saying to him?
phrases.notes: They should have raised the recognizable-leftovers objection instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's stated reason from Step 22 to question רבא's first approach from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the strict view requires recognizable leftovers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If recognizable leftovers were the real issue, the רבנן would have argued it against רבי מאיר. Instead they argued only about the flask bursting.

steps.title: The רבנן spoke first by their own view, then by רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the רבנן did hold the 'recognizable leftovers' rule. They only argued about the flask bursting because they were addressing רבי מאיר on his own terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they were saying to him: 'For us, we need תרומה that is a "first," whose leftovers can be recognized. For you —' (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 23 by rereading what the רבנן said to רבי מאיר. This passage stops in the middle of the sentence at 'for you —', so the second half of the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 asked why the רבנן did not raise the 'recognizable leftovers' argument against רבי מאיר. The answer is that this argument only works by their own view. רבי מאיר does not require it, so it would not convince him. The flask-bursting argument is what they would say according to his view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they were saying to him (a rereading of what was said)
According to us / our own view
According to you / your view
'First'; the Torah's word for תרומה, which implies it is taken from something
Its leftovers are recognizable

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן did not drop the 'recognizable leftovers' idea. They still hold it. They simply argued with רבי מאיר using an argument that would work even by his view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבא's first approach from Step 18, which he defended in Step 21. It shows that the רבנן's real reason can still be the 'recognizable leftovers' rule, even though the ברייתא records them talking about the flask bursting.

phrases.english: This is what they were saying to him:
phrases.notes: Signals that the גמרא is reinterpreting the רבנן's words in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: According to us — we require a 'first'
phrases.notes: The רבנן's own view: תרומה must be a 'first' taken from the produce.

phrases.english: whose leftovers are recognizable.
phrases.notes: The leftover part must be identifiable at the time of designation.

phrases.english: According to you —
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, with the argument about the flask bursting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of Step 23 by rereading the רבנן's words in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the dialogue as two layers: 'by our view' and 'by your view'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the רבנן argued only about the flask bursting, it seemed that 'recognizable leftovers' was not their reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן did hold the 'recognizable leftovers' requirement themselves. The flask argument was directed at רבי מאיר according to his own view.
